parsed.explanation: Combined regime: state law is strongly protective locally — anti-discrimination, hate-crime enhancement, X state ID, shield care — and the state has no mapped bathroom ban. That protection does not cancel federal entry, passport, facilities, or custody rules. Federal officers may refuse on document discrepancy and consider permanent fraud ineligibility, federal facilities are restricted by birth sex, and federal/immigration custody abuse and conversion-therapy practices are documented nationally. Admitted visitors face low local street/service risk, but every crossing and federal encounter carries universal document/facility exposure with severe custody tail-risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex definition; X/mismatched passports stopped Feb 2025 (existing X valid to expiry); cable directs refusal/refusal-plus-evidence on discrepancy and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; reports of confiscation/blocking/stranding; trans-athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: State X on licences/IDs since 2017 and birth certificates, no surgery requirement since 2014; ACLU suit and court challenges unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: State ID accessibility does not cure federal passport/visa screening; a discrepancy at entry can become fraud/detention exposure before state protections apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026 adopts conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs; stopped reporting trans prisoners; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse for trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Hate-crime enhancement applies to crimes, not custody placement; no documented trans custody protocol.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry/facilities arrest can route into federal/immigration custody where documented harm, not state anti-discrimination law, governs.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; state is among 29 with no mapped state bathroom ban, but federal buildings remain exposed.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public-accommodation/education/services law prohibits gender-identity discrimination since 2008, uniformly statewide; facilities law in this state not documented as banning identity-congruent use.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State-protected venues coexist with birth-sex federal facilities; traveller must navigate both systems depending on building ownership.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders describe youth gender care as mutilation, freeze funding, propose barring public insurance under 18, subpoena hospital records; emergency ward placement by federal marker not documented.
care_services.protection: 2023 shield law protects patients/providers from civil/criminal investigation for care legal in state but banned at home; public coverage of gender-affirming care for residents documented.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects care sought from state providers, but federal investigation/funding actions and document-based ward/facility assignment can still interrupt or expose care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal stance uses 'radical gender ideology'/'radically pro-transgender' in counterterrorism/reward guidance; orders to investigate/prosecute teachers aiding social transition; 66% poll support for birth-sex documents signals hostile national climate.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National employment ruling (2020) and hate-crimes statute remain; state hate-crime enhancement and 2021 panic-defence abolition documented; several federal orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State enforcement is protective, federal enforcement hostile; traveller faces federal threat-framing at borders/federal sites despite state law.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal sports ban, care-related orders, school 'gender ideology' investigations/prosecution directives, and June 2025 federal investigation of state over trans women in women's sports create guardian/minor exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law explicitly covers travelling patients/providers; inclusive schools policy upheld 2018-2020; conversion therapy on minors banned since 2015.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor can receive shielded state care/schooling while a parent/guardian faces federal investigation, sports/entry refusal, or document scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific data on police stops, searches, screening, or enforcement of public-accommodation law; national custody/police harassment documented but not quantified for this state.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State anti-discrimination, hate-crime enhancement, panic-defence abolition, and most-protective tier placement are documented protective signals; charging/prosecution statistics not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police response for street violence is not documented; absence is not treated as safety, and federal checkpoint/police exposure sits above local response.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and challenges to executive orders unresolved; several orders blocked/enjoined, making operative rule time-dependent; shield law narrowed in upper chamber, covered categories unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State courts, hate-crime penalties, shield law, and anti-discrimination law provide documented recourse locally; legal-aid FAQ on documents exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work best after admission in state systems; they do not reliably prevent federal refusal, permanent-ineligibility consideration, or custody harm in real time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35 because refusal is not a universal state-run register with no remedy: state protections, X state ID, shield law, hate-crime recourse and litigation operate, and imprisonment for presentation locally is not documented. Higher severity tail from federal fraud/custody keeps it near this band.

Similar to 0.55-B: extended secondary screening on document divergence, discretionary refusal and return rather than routine imprisonment, slow/uncertain appeals. We rate slightly below because the cable adds consideration of permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility and documented custody abuse, raising severity beyond administrative refusal.

Lower than 0.65-A: there, brief hold ended with apology/compensation and courts reliably ordered release. Here federal refusal/permanent-ineligibility consideration, birth-sex federal facilities, and unremedied custody practices mean remedies do not reliably restore the traveller in real time.

Well below 0.75-C: that anchor has matching-marker passports accepted, training, tribunal release and compensation, with only brief humiliating screening. Here X/mismatched documents are federally stopped/refusable, not routinely accepted.

parsed.synthesis: Interaction dominates: state protective machinery makes ordinary local life—housing, public accommodation, services, shielded care—materially safer than the national average, and is documented as operating by statute/tier. But the journey starts and can end in federal systems: passport/visa discrepancy to refusal or fraud consideration, federal birth-sex facilities, and federal/immigration custody with documented abuse. No documented pre-emption or immunity allows state law to cancel those exposures. Result is a split regime: low local severity if admitted, universal federal document/facility exposure with severe custody tail, mitigated but not offset by state protections and contested litigation.
